newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-BATTLING ALI-ROYAL LANDS SUSSEX STAKES.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-BATTLING ALI-ROYAL LANDS SUSSEX STAKES.

text.p: The 13-2 shot Ali-Royal, given a forceful ride by Kieren Fallon, on Wednesday won a battle royal with the favourite Starborough to win the Sussex Stakes, the Group One showpiece at the Glorious Goodwood meeting.
Trainer Henry Cecil, landing the Sussex Stakes for the fifth time, was all smiles afterwards and warmly applauded Fallon's hard-fought victory.
Cecil, harsh in condemnation of Fallon when he was beaten on Bosra Sham in the Eclipse Stakes, was fulsome in praise of his stable jockey this time.
"Kieren rode a great race on him and I am very pleased for him. It's a terrific day," said the dapper and elegant Cecil.
Ali-Royal, unlucky at Royal Asoct when he stumbled three furlongs out when challenging Allied Forces, made no mistake this time.
He hit the front about two furlongs out and came home the winner by three quarters of a length from Starborough, the much improved dual Group One winner who drifted in the betting to start at 9-4.
Third, a further three-quarters of a length back, came Allied Forces, who started at 9-2.
Fallon, riding his 101st winner of the season and setting a cracking pace at the head of the race for the jockeys' title, beamed with delight after his latest big race victory for the Cecil stable.
"I got the gaps and everything went his way. He picked up nice," the Irishman said of Ali-Royal, a son of the champion miler Royal Academy.

"When you are in front, you think the winning post is never going to come. But he is dead game," he said after Ali-Royal's plucky victory gained against the picturesque backdrop of the rolling Sussex Downs.
Pat Eddery took Starborough to the front as soon as the nine-horse field burst from the stalls, closely pursued by Gothenburg.
But Starborough, winner of the St James' Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot last time, could never shake off the field and dictate the pace as he likes.
The Irish 1,000 Guineas winner Classic Park got a dream of a run up the inside rail to challenge briefly for the lead in the straight, only to fade quickly.

Then Fallon, whip flailing as he hit the front, delivered the killer punch to Starborough's hopes to land the big race and leave wide open for the season the title of who can claim to be the best miler in Europe.
